1.sahih_international: Sad. By the Qur'an containing reminder...
1.yusuf_ali: Sad: By the Qur'an, Full of Admonition: (This is the Truth).
1.shakir: Suad, I swear by the Quran, full of admonition.
1.muhammad_sarwar: Sad. I swear by the Quran, which is full of reminders of God, (that you are a Messenger).
1.mohsin_khan: Sad [These letters (Sad etc.) are one of the miracles of the Quran and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings]. By the Quran full of reminding.
1.arberry: Sad. By the Koran, containing the Remembrance --

2.sahih_international: But those who disbelieve are in pride and dissension.
2.pickthall: Nay, but those who disbelieve are in false pride and schism.
2.yusuf_ali: But the Unbelievers (are steeped) in self-glory and Separatism.
2.shakir: Nay! those who disbelieve are in self-exaltation and opposition.
2.muhammad_sarwar: In fact, the unbelievers are the ones who are boastful and quarrelsome.
2.mohsin_khan: Nay, those who desbelieve are in false pride and opposition.
2.arberry: nay, but the unbelievers glory in their schism.

3.sahih_international: How many a generation have We destroyed before them, and they [then] called out; but it was not a time for escape.
3.pickthall: How many a generation We destroyed before them, and they cried out when it was no longer the time for escape!
3.yusuf_ali: How many generations before them did We destroy? In the end they cried (for mercy)- when there was no longer time for being saved!
3.shakir: How many did We destroy before them of the generations, then they cried while the time of escaping had passed away.
3.muhammad_sarwar: How many ancient generations did We destroy? (On facing Our torment) they cried out for help, but it was too late for them to escape.
3.mohsin_khan: How many a generation We have destroyed before them, and they cried out when there was no longer time for escape!
3.arberry: How many a generation We destroyed before them, and they called, but time was none to escape.

4.sahih_international: And they wonder that there has come to them a warner from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, "This is a magician and a liar.
4.pickthall: And they marvel that a warner from among themselves hath come unto them, and the disbelievers say: This is a wizard, a charlatan.
4.yusuf_ali: So they wonder that a Warner has come to them from among themselves! and the Unbelievers say, "This is a sorcerer telling lies!
4.shakir: And they wonder that there has come to them a warner from among themselves, and the disbelievers say: This is an enchanter, a liar.
4.muhammad_sarwar: It seems strange to the pagans that a man from their own people should come to them as a Prophet. The unbelievers have said, "He is only a lying magician".
4.mohsin_khan: And they (Arab pagans) wonder that a warner (Prophet Muhammad SAW) has come to them from among themselves! And the disbelievers say: "This (Prophet Muhammad SAW) is a sorcerer, a liar.
4.arberry: Now they marvel that a warner has come to them from among them; and the unbelievers say, 'This is a lying sorcerer.

5.sahih_international: Has he made the gods [only] one God? Indeed, this is a curious thing."
5.pickthall: Maketh he the gods One Allah? Lo! that is an astounding thing.
5.yusuf_ali: "Has he made the gods (all) into one Allah? Truly this is a wonderful thing!"
5.shakir: What! makes he the gods a single Allah? A strange thing is this, to be sure!
5.muhammad_sarwar: They say, "Has he condemned all other gods but One? This is certainly strange".
5.mohsin_khan: "Has he made the aliha (gods) (all) into One Ilah (God - Allah). Verily, this is a curious thing!"
5.arberry: What, has he made the gods One God? This is indeed a marvellous thing.'

6.sahih_international: And the eminent among them went forth, [saying], "Continue, and be patient over [the defense of] your gods. Indeed, this is a thing intended.
6.pickthall: The chiefs among them go about, exhorting: Go and be staunch to your gods! Lo! this is a thing designed.
6.yusuf_ali: And the leader among them go away (impatiently), (saying), "Walk ye away, and remain constant to your gods! For this is truly a thing designed (against you)!
6.shakir: And the chief persons of them break forth, saying: Go and steadily adhere to your gods; this is most surely a thing sought after.
6.muhammad_sarwar: A group of the pagans walked out of a meeting with the Prophet and told the others, "Let us walk away. Be steadfast in the worship of your gods. This man wants to dominate you.
6.mohsin_khan: And the leaders among them went about (saying): "Go on, and remain constant to your aliha (gods)! Verily, This is a thing designed (against you)!
6.arberry: And the Council of them depart, saying 'Go! Be steadfast to your gods; this is a thing to be desired.

7.sahih_international: We have not heard of this in the latest religion. This is not but a fabrication.
7.pickthall: We have not heard of this in later religion. This is naught but an invention.
7.yusuf_ali: "We never heard (the like) of this among the people of these latter days: this is nothing but a made-up tale!"
7.shakir: We never heard of this in the former faith; this is nothing but a forgery:
7.muhammad_sarwar: We have heard nothing like this in the latest religion. This is only his own false invention.
7.mohsin_khan: "We have not heard (the like) of this among the people of these later days. This is nothing but an invention!
7.arberry: We have not heard of this in the last religion; this is surely an invention.

8.sahih_international: Has the message been revealed to him out of [all of] us?" Rather, they are in doubt about My message. Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment.
8.pickthall: Hath the reminder been unto him (alone) among us? Nay, but they are in doubt concerning My reminder; nay but they have not yet tasted My doom.
8.yusuf_ali: "What! has the Message been sent to him - (Of all persons) among us?"... but they are in doubt concerning My (Own) Message! Nay, they have not yet tasted My Punishment!
8.shakir: Has the reminder been revealed to him from among us? Nay! they are in doubt as to My reminder. Nay! they have not yet tasted My chastisement!
8.muhammad_sarwar: Can it be that he alone has received the Quran?" In fact, they have doubts about My Quran and this is because they have not yet faced (My) torment.
8.mohsin_khan: "Has the Reminder been sent down to him (alone) from among us?" Nay! but they are in doubt about My Reminder (this Quran)! Nay, but they have not tasted (My) Torment!
8.arberry: What, has the Remembrance been sent down on him out of us all?' Nay, but they are in doubt of My Remembrance; nay, they have not yet tasted My chastisement.

9.sahih_international: Or do they have the depositories of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower?
9.pickthall: Or are theirs the treasures of the mercy of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower?
9.yusuf_ali: Or have they the treasures of the mercy of thy Lord,- the Exalted in Power, the Grantor of Bounties without measure?
9.shakir: Or is it that they have the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Mighty, the great Giver?
9.muhammad_sarwar: Do they possess the treasures of the mercy of your, (Muhammad's), Lord, the Majestic and Munificent God?
9.mohsin_khan: Or have they the treasures of the Mercy of your Lord, the All-Mighty, the Real Bestower?
9.arberry: Or have they the treasuries of thy Lord's mercy, the All-mighty, the All-giving?

10.sahih_international: Or is theirs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend through [any] ways of access.
10.pickthall: Or is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them theirs? Then let them ascend by ropes!
10.yusuf_ali: Or have they the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all between? If so, let them mount up with the ropes and means (to reach that end)!
10.shakir: Or is it that theirs is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend by any
10.muhammad_sarwar: Do they own the heavens and the earth and all that is between them? Let them try on their own to block (the ways of heavens so that Our revelations cannot come to you).
10.mohsin_khan: Or is it that the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them is theirs? If so, let them ascend up with means (to the heavens)!
10.arberry: Or is theirs the kingdom of the heavens and earth and of what between them is? Why, then let them ascend the cords!

11.sahih_international: [They are but] soldiers [who will be] defeated there among the companies [of disbelievers].
11.pickthall: A defeated host are (all) the factions that are there.
11.yusuf_ali: But there - will be put to flight even a host of confederates.
11.shakir: A host of deserters of the allies shall be here put to flight.
11.muhammad_sarwar: They are only a small band among the defeated confederate tribes.
11.mohsin_khan: (As they denied Allah's Message) they will be a defeated host like the confederates of the old times (who were defeated).
11.arberry: A very host of parties is routed there!

12.sahih_international: The people of Noah denied before them, and [the tribe of] 'Aad and Pharaoh, the owner of stakes,
12.pickthall: The folk of Noah before them denied (their messenger) and (so did the tribe of) A'ad, and Pharaoh firmly planted,
12.yusuf_ali: Before them (were many who) rejected messengers,- the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh, the Lord of Stakes,
12.shakir: The people of Nuh and Ad, and Firon, the lord of spikes, rejected (apostles) before them.
12.muhammad_sarwar: The people of Noah, Ad and the dominating Pharaoh had rejected Our revelations.
12.mohsin_khan: Before them (were many who) belied Messengers, the people of Nuh (Noah); and 'Ad; and Fir'aun (Pharaoh) the man of stakes (with which he used to punish the people),
12.arberry: Cried lies before them the people of Noah, and Ad, and Pharaoh, he of the tent-pegs,

13.sahih_international: And [the tribe of] Thamud and the people of Lot and the companions of the thicket. Those are the companies.
13.pickthall: And (the tribe of) Thamud, and the folk of Lot, and the dwellers in the wood: these were the factions.
13.yusuf_ali: And Thamud, and the people of Lut, and the Companions of the Wood; - such were the Confederates.
13.shakir: And Samood and the people of Lut and the dwellers of the thicket; these were the parties.
13.muhammad_sarwar: So also did the people of Thamud, Lot, and the dwellers of the Forest.
13.mohsin_khan: And Thamud, and the people of Lout (Lot), and the dwellers of the wood; such were the confederates.
13.arberry: and Thamood, and the people of Lot, and the men of the Thicket - those were the parties;

14.sahih_international: Each of them denied the messengers, so My penalty was justified.
14.pickthall: Not one of them but did deny the messengers, therefor My doom was justified,
14.yusuf_ali: Not one (of them) but rejected the messengers, but My punishment came justly and inevitably (on them).
14.shakir: There was none of them but called the apostles liars, so just was My retribution.
14.muhammad_sarwar: Each of them who rejected the Messenger become subject to Our punishment.
14.mohsin_khan: Not one of them but belied the Messengers, therefore My Torment was justified,
14.arberry: not one, that cried not lies to the Messengers, so My retribution was just.

15.sahih_international: And these [disbelievers] await not but one blast [of the Horn]; for it there will be no delay.
15.pickthall: These wait for but one Shout, there will be no second thereto.
15.yusuf_ali: These (today) only wait for a single mighty Blast, which (when it comes) will brook no delay.
15.shakir: Nor do these await aught but a single cry, there being no delay in it.
15.muhammad_sarwar: They had only to wait for the single inevitable blast.
15.mohsin_khan: And these only wait for a single Saihah [shout (i.e. the blowing of the Trumpet by the angel Israfil Sarafil)] there will be no pause or ending thereto [till everything will perish except Allah (the only God full of Majesty, Bounty and Honour)].
15.arberry: These are only awaiting for a single Cry, to which there is no delay.

16.sahih_international: And they say, "Our Lord, hasten for us our share [of the punishment] before the Day of Account"
16.pickthall: They say: Our Lord! Hasten on for us our fate before the Day of Reckoning.
16.yusuf_ali: They say: "Our Lord! hasten to us our sentence (even) before the Day of Account!"
16.shakir: And they say: O our Lord! hasten on to us our portion before the day of reckoning.
16.muhammad_sarwar: They scornfully said, "Lord, show us the record of our deeds before the day when everyone must present the account of their deeds.".
16.mohsin_khan: They say: "Our Lord! Hasten to us Qittana (i.e. our Record of good and bad deeds so that we see it) before the Day of Reckoning!"
16.arberry: They say, 'Our Lord, hasten to us our share before the Day of Reckoning.'

17.sahih_international: Be patient over what they say and remember Our servant, David, the possessor of strength; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah].
17.pickthall: Bear with what they say, and remember Our bondman David, lord of might, Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah).
17.yusuf_ali: Have patience at what they say, and remember our servant David, the man of strength: for he ever turned (to Allah).
17.shakir: Bear patiently what they say, and remember Our servant Dawood, the possessor of power; surely he was frequent in returning (to Allah).
17.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), bear patiently what they say and recall Our servant, David, who had strong hands and who was most repentant.
17.mohsin_khan: Be patient (O Muhammad SAW) of what they say, and remember Our slave Dawud (David), endued with power. Verily, he was ever oft-returning in all matters and in repentance (toward Allah).
17.arberry: Bear patiently what they say, and remember Our servant David, the man of might; he was a penitent.

18.sahih_international: Indeed, We subjected the mountains [to praise] with him, exalting [Allah] in the [late] afternoon and [after] sunrise.
18.pickthall: Lo! We subdued the hills to hymn the praises (of their Lord) with him at nightfall and sunrise,
18.yusuf_ali: It was We that made the hills declare, in unison with him, Our Praises, at eventide and at break of day,
18.shakir: Surely We made the mountains to sing the glory (of Allah) in unison with him at the evening and the sunrise,
18.muhammad_sarwar: We made the mountains join him in glorifying Us in the evening and in the morning.
18.mohsin_khan: Verily, We made the mountains to glorify Our Praises with him [Dawud (David)] in the 'Ashi (i.e. after the mid-day till sunset) and Ishraq (i.e. after the sunrise till mid-day).
18.arberry: With him We subjected the mountains to give glory at evening and sunrise,

19.sahih_international: And the birds were assembled, all with him repeating [praises].
19.pickthall: And the birds assembled; all were turning unto Him.
19.yusuf_ali: And the birds gathered (in assemblies): all with him did turn (to Allah).
19.shakir: And the birds gathered together; all joined in singing with him.
19.muhammad_sarwar: We made the birds assemble around him in flocks.
19.mohsin_khan: And (so did) the birds assembled: all with him [Dawud (David)] did turn (to Allah i.e. glorified His Praises).
19.arberry: and the birds, duly mustered, every one to him reverting;

20.sahih_international: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and discernment in speech.
20.pickthall: We made his kingdom strong and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.
20.yusuf_ali: We strengthened his kingdom, and gave him wisdom and sound judgment in speech and decision.
20.shakir: And We strengthened his kingdom and We gave him wisdom and a clear judgment.
20.muhammad_sarwar: We strengthened his kingdom, giving him wisdom and the power of sound Judgment.
20.mohsin_khan: We made his kingdom strong and gave him Al-Hikmah (Prophethood, etc.) and sound judgement in speech and decision.
20.arberry: We strengthened his kingdom, and gave him wisdom and speech decisive.

21.sahih_international: And has there come to you the news of the adversaries, when they climbed over the wall of [his] prayer chamber -
21.pickthall: And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee? How they climbed the wall into the royal chamber;
21.yusuf_ali: Has the Story of the Disputants reached thee? Behold, they climbed over the wall of the private chamber;
21.shakir: And has there come to you the story of the litigants, when they made an entry into the private chamber by ascending over the walls?
21.muhammad_sarwar: Have you heard the news of the disputing parties who climbed the walls of the prayer room
21.mohsin_khan: And has the news of the litigants reached you? When they climbed over the wall into (his) Mihrab (a praying place or a private room,).
21.arberry: Has the tiding of the dispute come to thee? When they scaled the Sanctuary,

22.sahih_international: When they entered upon David and he was alarmed by them? They said, "Fear not. [We are] two adversaries, one of whom has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not exceed [it] and guide us to the sound path.
22.pickthall: How they burst in upon David, and he was afraid of them. They said: Be not afraid! (We are) two litigants, one of whom hath wronged the other, therefor judge aright between us; be not unjust; and show us the fair way.
22.yusuf_ali: When they entered the presence of David, and he was terrified of them, they said: "Fear not: we are two disputants, one of whom has wronged the other: Decide now between us with truth, and treat us not with injustice, but guide us to the even Path..
22.shakir: When they entered in upon Dawood and he was frightened at them, they said: Fear not; two litigants, of whom one has acted wrongfully towards the other, therefore decide between us with justice, and do not act unjustly, and guide us to the right way.
22.muhammad_sarwar: and entered where David was (praying). He was frightened, so they said, "Do not be afraid. We are only two disputing parties of which one of us has transgressed against the other. Judge between us with truth and justice and guide us to the right path".
22.mohsin_khan: When they entered in upon Dawud (David), he was terrified of them, they said: "Fear not! (We are) two litigants, one of whom has wronged the other, therefore judge between us with truth, and treat us not with injustice, and guide us to the Right Way.
22.arberry: when they entered upon David, and he took fright at them; and they said, 'Fear not; two disputants we are -- one of us has injured the other; so judge between us justly, and transgress not, and guide us to the right path.'

23.sahih_international: Indeed this, my brother, has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe; so he said, 'Entrust her to me,' and he overpowered me in speech."
23.pickthall: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech.
23.yusuf_ali: "This man is my brother: He has nine and ninety ewes, and I have (but) one: Yet he says, 'commit her to my care,' and is (moreover) harsh to me in speech."
23.shakir: Surely this is my brother; he has ninety-nine ewes and I have a single ewe; but he said: Make it over to me, and he has prevailed against me in discourse.
23.muhammad_sarwar: One of them said, "This is my brother who has ninety-nine ewes when I have only one. He has demanded me to place that one in his custody; he had the stronger argument".
23.mohsin_khan: Verily, this my brother (in religion) has ninety nine ewes, while I have (only) one ewe, and he says: "Hand it over to me, and he overpowered me in speech."
23.arberry: 'Behold, this my brother has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe. So he said, "Give her into my charge"; and he overcame me in the argument.'

24.sahih_international: [David] said, "He has certainly wronged you in demanding your ewe [in addition] to his ewes. And indeed, many associates oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - and few are they." And David became certain that We had tried him, and he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned in repentance [to Allah].
24.pickthall: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented.
24.yusuf_ali: (David) said: "He has undoubtedly wronged thee in demanding thy (single) ewe to be added to his (flock of) ewes: truly many are the partners (in business) who wrong each other: Not so do those who believe and work deeds of righteousness, and how few are they?"... and David gathered that We had tried him: he asked forgiveness of his Lord, fell down, bowing (in prostration), and turned (to Allah in repentance).
24.shakir: He said: Surely he has been unjust to you in demanding your ewe (to add) to his own ewes; and most surely most of the partners act wrongfully towards one another, save those who believe and do good, and very few are they; and Dawood was sure that We had tried him, so he sought the protection of his Lord and he fell down bowing and turned time after time (to Him).
24.muhammad_sarwar: David said, "He has certainly been unjust in demanding your ewe from you. Most partners transgress against each other except for the righteously striving believers who are very few." David realized that it was a test from Us so he asked forgiveness from his Lord and knelt down before him in repentance.
24.mohsin_khan: [Dawud (David)] said (immediately without listening to the opponent): "He has wronged you in demanding your ewe in addition to his ewes. And, verily, many partners oppress one another, except those who believe and do righteous good deeds, and they are few." And Dawud (David) guessed that We have tried him and he sought Forgiveness of his Lord, and he fell down prostrate and turned (to Allah) in repentance.
24.arberry: Said he, 'Assuredly he has wronged thee in asking for thy ewe in addition to his sheep; and indeed many intermixers do injury one against the other, save those who believe, and do deeds of righteousness -- and how few they are!' And David thought that We had only tried him; therefore he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he fell down, bowing, and he repented.

25.sahih_international: So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
25.pickthall: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey's end.
25.yusuf_ali: So We forgave him this (lapse): he enjoyed, indeed, a Near Approach to Us, and a beautiful place of (Final) Return.
25.shakir: Therefore We rectified for him this, and most surely he had a nearness to Us and an excellent resort.
25.muhammad_sarwar: We forgave him for this. In Our eyes he certainly has a good position and the best share (of the world to come).
25.mohsin_khan: So We forgave him that, and verily, for him is a near access to Us, and a good place of (final) return (Paradise).
25.arberry: Accordingly We forgave him that, and he has a near place in Our presence and a fair resort.

26.sahih_international: [We said], "O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, as it will lead you astray from the way of Allah." Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account.
26.pickthall: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning.
26.yusuf_ali: O David! We did indeed make thee a vicegerent on earth: so judge thou between men in truth (and justice): Nor follow thou the lusts (of thy heart), for they will mislead thee from the Path of Allah: for those who wander astray from the Path of Allah, is a Penalty Grievous, for that they forget the Day of Account.
26.shakir: o Dawood! surely We have made you a ruler in the land; so judge between men with justice and do not follow desire, lest it should lead you astray from the path of Allah; (as for) those who go astray from the path of Allah, they shall surely have a severe punishment because they forgot the day of reckoning.
26.muhammad_sarwar: We told him. "David, We have appointed you as Our deputy on earth so judge among the people with truth. Do not follow (worldly) desires lest you go astray from the way of God. Those who go astray from the way of God will suffer severe torment for forgetting the Day of Reckoning.
26.mohsin_khan: O Dawud (David)! Verily! We have placed you as a successor on earth, so judge you between men in truth (and justice) and follow not your desire for it will mislead you from the Path of Allah. Verily! Those who wander astray from the Path of Allah (shall) have a severe torment, because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.
26.arberry: 'David, behold, We have appointed thee a viceroy in the earth; therefore judge between men justly, and follow not caprice, lest it lead thee astray from the way of God. Surely those who go astray from the way of God -- there awaits them a terrible chastisement, for that they have forgotten the Day of Reckoning.'

27.sahih_international: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and that between them aimlessly. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.
27.pickthall: And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the opinion of those who disbelieve. And woe unto those who disbelieve, from the Fire!
27.yusuf_ali: Not without purpose did We create heaven and earth and all between! that were the thought of Unbelievers! but woe to the Unbelievers because of the Fire (of Hell)!
27.shakir: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain; that is the opinion of those who disbelieve then woe to those who disbelieve on account of the fire.
27.muhammad_sarwar: We have not created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them without purpose, even though this is the belief of the disbelievers. Woe to the disbelievers; they will suffer the torment of fire
27.mohsin_khan: And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them without purpose! That is the consideration of those who disbelieve! Then woe to those who disbelieve (in Islamic Monotheism) from the Fire!
27.arberry: We have not created the heavens and earth, and what between them is, for vanity; such is the thought of the unbelievers, wherefore woe unto the unbelievers because of the Fire!

28.sahih_international: Or should we treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters in the land? Or should We treat those who fear Allah like the wicked?
28.pickthall: Shall We treat those who believe and do good works as those who spread corruption in the earth; or shall We treat the pious as the wicked?
28.yusuf_ali: Shall We treat those who believe and work deeds of righteousness, the same as those who do mischief on earth? Shall We treat those who guard against evil, the same as those who turn aside from the right?
28.shakir: Shall We treat those who believe and do good like the mischief-makers in the earth? Or shall We make those who guard (against evil) like the wicked?
28.muhammad_sarwar: Do We consider the righteously striving believers equal to the evil-doers in the land? Are the pious ones equal to those who openly commit sin?
28.mohsin_khan: Shall We treat those who believe (in the Oneness of Allah Islamic Monotheism) and do righteous good deeds, as Mufsidun (those who associate partners in worship with Allah and commit crimes) on earth? Or shall We treat the Muttaqun (pious - see V. 2:2), as the Fujjar (criminals, disbelievers, wicked, etc)?
28.arberry: Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds as the workers of corruption in the earth, or shall We make the godfearing as the transgressors?

29.sahih_international: [This is] a blessed Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that they might reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding would be reminded.
29.pickthall: (This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect.
29.yusuf_ali: (Here is) a Book which We have sent down unto thee, full of blessings, that they may mediate on its Signs, and that men of understanding may receive admonition.
29.shakir: (It is) a Book We have revealed to you abounding in good that they may ponder over its verses, and that those endowed with understanding may be mindful.
29.muhammad_sarwar: It is a blessed Book which We have revealed for you so that you will reflect upon its verses and so the people of understanding will take heed.
29.mohsin_khan: (This is) a Book (the Quran) which We have sent down to you, full of blessings that they may ponder over its Verses, and that men of understanding may remember.
29.arberry: A Book We have sent down to thee, Blessed, that men possessed of minds may ponder its signs and so remember.

30.sahih_international: And to David We gave Solomon. An excellent servant, indeed he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allah].
30.pickthall: And We bestowed on David, Solomon. How excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah).
30.yusuf_ali: To David We gave Solomon (for a son),- How excellent in Our service! Ever did he turn (to Us)!
30.shakir: And We gave to Dawood Sulaiman, most excellent the servant! Surely he was frequent in returning (to Allah).
30.muhammad_sarwar: We granted Solomon to David, a blessed servant of Ours and certainly the most repentant person.
30.mohsin_khan: And to Dawud (David) We gave Sulaiman (Solomon). How excellent (a) slave! Verily, he was ever oft-returning in repentance (to Us)!
30.arberry: And We gave unto David Solomon; how excellent a servant he was! He was a penitent.

31.sahih_international: [Mention] when there were exhibited before him in the afternoon the poised [standing] racehorses.
31.pickthall: When there were shown to him at eventide lightfooted coursers
31.yusuf_ali: Behold, there were brought before him, at eventide coursers of the highest breeding, and swift of foot;
31.shakir: When there were brought to him in the evening (horses) still when standing, swift when running--
31.muhammad_sarwar: When the noble galloping horses were displayed to him one evening,
31.mohsin_khan: When there were displayed before him, in the afternoon, well trained horses of the highest breed [for Jihad (holy fighting in Allah's Cause)].
31.arberry: When in the evening were presented to him the standing steeds,

32.sahih_international: And he said, "Indeed, I gave preference to the love of good [things] over the remembrance of my Lord until the sun disappeared into the curtain [of darkness]."
32.pickthall: And he said: Lo! I have preferred the good things (of the world) to the remembrance of my Lord; till they were taken out of sight behind the curtain.
32.yusuf_ali: And he said, "Truly do I love the love of good, with a view to the glory of my Lord,"- until (the sun) was hidden in the veil (of night):
32.shakir: Then he said: Surely I preferred the good things to the remembrance of my Lord-- until the sun set and time for Asr prayer was over, (he said):
32.muhammad_sarwar: he said, "My love of horses for the cause of God has made me continue watching them until sunset, thus making me miss my prayer".
32.mohsin_khan: And he said: "Alas! I did love the good (these horses) instead of remembering my Lord (in my 'Asr prayer)" till the time was over, and (the sun) had hidden in the veil (of night).
32.arberry: he said, 'Lo, I have loved the love of good things better than the remembrance of my Lord, until the sun was bidden behind the veil.

33.sahih_international: [He said], "Return them to me," and set about striking [their] legs and necks.
33.pickthall: (Then he said): Bring them back to me, and fell to slashing (with his sword their) legs and necks.
33.yusuf_ali: "Bring them back to me." then began he to pass his hand over (their) legs and their necks.
33.shakir: Bring them back to me; so he began to slash (their) legs and necks.
33.muhammad_sarwar: He said, "Bring them back to me." Then he started to rub their legs and necks.
33.mohsin_khan: Then he said "Bring them (horses) back to me." Then he began to pass his hand over their legs and their necks (till the end of the display).
33.arberry: Return them to me!' And he began to stroke their shanks and necks.

34.sahih_international: And We certainly tried Solomon and placed on his throne a body; then he returned.
34.pickthall: And verily We tried Solomon, and set upon his throne a (mere) body. Then did he repent.
34.yusuf_ali: And We did try Solomon: We placed on his throne a body (without life); but he did turn (to Us in true devotion):
34.shakir: And certainly We tried Sulaiman, and We put on his throne a (mere) body, so he turned (to Allah).
34.muhammad_sarwar: We tested Solomon by (causing death to his son) and leaving his body on Solomon's chair. Then he turned to Us in repentance,
34.mohsin_khan: And, indeed We did try Sulaiman (Solomon) and We placed on his throne Jasadan (a devil, so he lost his kingdom for a while) but he did return (to his throne and kingdom by the Grace of Allah and he did return) to Allah with obedience and in repentance.
34.arberry: Certainly We tried Solomon, and We cast upon his throne a mere body; then he repented.

35.sahih_international: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."
35.pickthall: He said: My Lord! Forgive me and bestow on me sovereignty such as shall not belong to any after me. Lo! Thou art the Bestower.
35.yusuf_ali: He said, "O my Lord! Forgive me, and grant me a kingdom which, (it may be), suits not another after me: for Thou art the Grantor of Bounties (without measure).
35.shakir: He said: My Lord! do Thou forgive me and grant me a kingdom which is not fit for (being inherited by) anyone after me;
35.muhammad_sarwar: saying, "Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that no one after me can have the like. You are All-munificent".
35.mohsin_khan: He said: "My Lord! Forgive me, and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not belong to any other after me: Verily, You are the Bestower."
35.arberry: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me, and give me a kingdom such as may not befall anyone after me; surely Thou art the All-giver.'

36.sahih_international: So We subjected to him the wind blowing by his command, gently, wherever he directed,
36.pickthall: So We made the wind subservient unto him, setting fair by his command whithersoever he intended.
36.yusuf_ali: Then We subjected the wind to his power, to flow gently to his order, Whithersoever he willed,-
36.shakir: Then We made the wind subservient to him; it made his command to run gently wherever he desired,
36.muhammad_sarwar: We made the wind subservient to him, to blow gently wherever he desired at his command
36.mohsin_khan: So, We subjected to him the wind, it blew gently to his order whithersoever he willed,
36.arberry: So We subjected to him the wind, that ran at his commandment, softly, wherever he might light on,

37.sahih_international: And [also] the devils [of jinn] - every builder and diver
37.pickthall: And the unruly, every builder and diver (made We subservient),
37.yusuf_ali: As also the evil ones, (including) every kind of builder and diver,-
37.shakir: And the shaitans, every builder and diver,
37.muhammad_sarwar: and all the devils who built and dived for him.
37.mohsin_khan: And also the Shayatin (devils) from the jinns (including) every kind of builder and diver,
37.arberry: and the Satans, every builder and diver

38.sahih_international: And others bound together in shackles.
38.pickthall: And others linked together in chains,
38.yusuf_ali: As also others bound together in fetters.
38.muhammad_sarwar: The rest of the devils were bound in chains.
38.mohsin_khan: And also others bound in fetters.
38.arberry: and others also, coupled in fetters:

39.sahih_international: [We said], "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account."
39.pickthall: (Saying): This is Our gift, so bestow thou, or withhold, without reckoning.
39.yusuf_ali: "Such are Our Bounties: whether thou bestow them (on others) or withhold them, no account will be asked."
39.shakir: This is Our free gift, therefore give freely or withhold, without reckoning.
39.muhammad_sarwar: We told him, "This is Our gift to you so give them away free or keep them as you like".
39.mohsin_khan: [Saying of Allah to Sulaiman (Solomon)]: "This is Our gift, so spend you or withhold, no account will be asked."
39.arberry: 'This is Our gift; bestow or withhold without reckoning.'

40.sahih_international: And indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
40.pickthall: And lo! he hath favour with Us, and a happy journey's end.
40.yusuf_ali: And he enjoyed, indeed, a Near Approach to Us, and a beautiful Place of (Final) Return.
40.shakir: And most surely he had a nearness to Us and an excellent resort.
40.muhammad_sarwar: In Our eyes he certainly has a high position and the best place to return.
40.mohsin_khan: And verily, he enjoyed a near access to Us, and a good final return (Paradise).
40.arberry: And he had a near place in Our presence and a fair resort.

41.sahih_international: And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."
41.pickthall: And make mention (O Muhammad) of Our bondman Job, when he cried unto his Lord (saying): Lo! the devil doth afflict me with distress and torment.
41.yusuf_ali: Commemorate Our Servant Job. Behold he cried to his Lord: "The Evil One has afflicted me with distress and suffering!"
41.shakir: And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called upon his Lord: The Shaitan has afflicted me with toil and torment.
41.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), recall Our servant Job. When he prayed to his Lord saying, "Satan has afflicted me with hardship and torment,"
41.mohsin_khan: And remember Our slave Ayub (Job), when he invoked his Lord (saying): "Verily! Shaitan (Satan) has touched me with distress (by losing my health) and torment (by losing my wealth)!
41.arberry: Remember also Our servant Job; when he called to his Lord, 'Behold, Satan has visited me with weariness and chastisement.'

42.sahih_international: [So he was told], "Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a [spring for] a cool bath and drink."
42.pickthall: (And it was said unto him): Strike the ground with thy foot. This (spring) is a cool bath and a refreshing drink.
42.yusuf_ali: (The command was given:) "Strike with thy foot: here is (water) wherein to wash, cool and refreshing, and (water) to drink."
42.shakir: Urge with your foot; here is a cool washing-place and a drink.
42.muhammad_sarwar: (We answered his prayer, healed his sickness, and told him), "Run on your feet. This is cool water (for you) to wash and drink".
42.mohsin_khan: (Allah said to him): "Strike the ground with your foot: This is a spring of water to wash in, cool and a (refreshing) drink."
42.arberry: 'Stamp thy foot! This is a laving-place cool, and a drink.'

43.sahih_international: And We granted him his family and a like [number] with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.
43.pickthall: And We bestowed on him (again) his household and therewith the like thereof, a mercy from Us, and a memorial for men of understanding.
43.yusuf_ali: And We gave him (back) his people, and doubled their number,- as a Grace from Ourselves, and a thing for commemoration, for all who have Understanding.
43.shakir: And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us, and as a reminder to those possessed of understanding.
43.muhammad_sarwar: We gave him back his family and doubled their number as a blessing from Us and as a reminder to the people of understanding.
43.mohsin_khan: And We gave him (back) his family, and along with them the like thereof, as a Mercy from Us, and a Reminder for those who understand.
43.arberry: And We gave to him his family, and the like of them with them, as a mercy from us, and a reminder unto men possessed of minds;

44.sahih_international: [We said], "And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath." Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allah].
44.pickthall: And (it was said unto him): Take in thine hand a branch and smite therewith, and break not thine oath. Lo! We found him steadfast, how excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (to his Lord).
44.yusuf_ali: "And take in thy hand a little grass, and strike therewith: and break not (thy oath)." Truly We found him full of patience and constancy. How excellent in Our service! ever did he turn (to Us)!
44.shakir: And take in your hand a green branch and beat her with It and do not break your oath; surely We found him patient; most excellent the servant! Surely he was frequent in returning (to Allah).
44.muhammad_sarwar: We told him, "Take a handful of straw. Strike your wife with it to fulfill your oath." We found him to be patient. What an excellent servant he was. He was certainly most repenting.
44.mohsin_khan: "And take in your hand a bundle of thin grass and strike therewith (your wife), and break not your oath. Truly! We found him patient. How excellent (a) slave! Verily, he was ever oft-returning in repentance (to Us)!
44.arberry: and, 'Take in thy hand a bundle of rushes, and strike therewith, and do not fail in thy oath.' Surely We found him a steadfast man. How excellent a servant he was! He was a penitent.

45.sahih_international: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob - those of strength and [religious] vision.
45.pickthall: And make mention of Our bondmen, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, men of parts and vision.
45.yusuf_ali: And commemorate Our Servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, possessors of Power and Vision.
45.shakir: And remember Our servants Ibrahim and Ishaq and Yaqoub, men of power and insight.
45.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), recall Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, all of whom possessed virtuous hands and clear visions.
45.mohsin_khan: And remember Our slaves, Ibrahim (Abraham), Ishaque (Isaac), and Ya'qub (Jacob), (all) owners of strength (in worshipping Us) and (also) of religious understanding.
45.arberry: Remember also Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob -- men of might they and of vision.

46.sahih_international: Indeed, We chose them for an exclusive quality: remembrance of the home [of the Hereafter].
46.pickthall: Lo! We purified them with a pure thought, remembrance of the Home (of the Hereafter).
46.yusuf_ali: Verily We did choose them for a special (purpose)- proclaiming the Message of the Hereafter.
46.shakir: Surely We purified them by a pure quality, the keeping in mind of the (final) abode.
46.muhammad_sarwar: We gave them this pure distinction because of their continual remembrance of the Day of Judgment.
46.mohsin_khan: Verily, We did choose them by granting them (a good thing, i.e.) the remembrance of the home [in the Hereafter and they used to make the people remember it, and also they used to invite the people to obey Allah and to do good deeds for the Hereafter].
46.arberry: Assuredly We purified them with a quality most pure, the remembrance of the Abode,

47.sahih_international: And indeed they are, to Us, among the chosen and outstanding.
47.pickthall: Lo! in Our sight they are verily of the elect, the excellent.
47.yusuf_ali: They were, in Our sight, truly, of the company of the Elect and the Good.
47.shakir: And most surely they were with Us, of the elect, the best.
47.muhammad_sarwar: In Our eyes they were of the chosen, virtuous people.
47.mohsin_khan: And they are with Us, verily, of the chosen and the best!
47.arberry: and in Our sight they are of the chosen, the excellent.

48.sahih_international: And remember Ishmael, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding.
48.pickthall: And make mention of Ishmael and Elisha and Dhu'l-Kifl. All are of the chosen.
48.yusuf_ali: And commemorate Isma'il, Elisha, and Zul-Kifl: Each of them was of the Company of the Good.
48.shakir: And remember Ismail and Al-Yasha and Zulkifl; and they were all of the best.
48.muhammad_sarwar: Recall Ismael, Elisha, and Dhulkifl (Ezekiel) who were all virtuous people.
48.mohsin_khan: And remember Isma'il (Ishmael), Al-Yasa'a (Elisha), and Dhul-Kifl (Isaiah), all are among the best.
48.arberry: Remember also Our servants Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul Kifl; each is among the excellent.

49.sahih_international: This is a reminder. And indeed, for the righteous is a good place of return
49.pickthall: This is a reminder. And lo! for those who ward off (evil) is a happy journey's end,
49.yusuf_ali: This is a Message (of admonition): and verily, for the righteous, is a beautiful Place of (Final) Return,-
49.shakir: This is a reminder; and most surely there is an excellent resort for those who guard (against evil),
49.muhammad_sarwar: Such is their noble story. The pious ones will certainly have the best place to return.
49.mohsin_khan: This is a Reminder, and verily, for the Muttaqun (pious and righteous persons - see V. 2:2) is a good final return (Paradise),
49.arberry: This is a Remembrance; and for the godfearing is a fair resort,

50.sahih_international: Gardens of perpetual residence, whose doors will be opened to them.
50.pickthall: Gardens of Eden, whereof the gates are opened for them,
50.yusuf_ali: Gardens of Eternity, whose doors will (ever) be open to them;
50.shakir: The gardens of perpetuity, the doors are opened for them.
50.muhammad_sarwar: They will enter gardens of Eden with their gates open for them.
50.mohsin_khan: 'Adn (Edn) Paradise (everlasting Gardens), whose doors will be open for them, [It is said (in Tafsir At-Tabari, Part 23, Page 174) that one can speak to the doors, just one tells it to open and close, and it will open or close as it is ordered].
50.arberry: Gardens of Eden, whereof the gates are open to them,

51.sahih_international: Reclining within them, they will call therein for abundant fruit and drink.
51.pickthall: Wherein, reclining, they call for plenteous fruit and cool drink (that is) therein.
51.yusuf_ali: Therein will they recline (at ease): Therein can they call (at pleasure) for fruit in abundance, and (delicious) drink;
51.shakir: Reclining therein, calling therein for many fruits and drink.
51.muhammad_sarwar: They will be resting therein and will be able to ask for many kinds of fruit and drink.
51.mohsin_khan: Therein they will recline; therein they will call for fruits in abundance and drinks;
51.arberry: wherein they recline, and wherein they call for fruits abundant, and sweet potions,

52.sahih_international: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances and of equal age.
52.pickthall: And with them are those of modest gaze, companions.
52.yusuf_ali: And beside them will be chaste women restraining their glances, (companions) of equal age.
52.shakir: And with them shall be those restraining their eyes, equals in age.
52.muhammad_sarwar: They will have bashful wives of equal age with them.
52.mohsin_khan: And beside them will be chaste females (virgins) restraining their glances only for their husbands, (and) of equal ages.
52.arberry: and with them maidens restraining their glances of equal age.

53.sahih_international: This is what you, [the righteous], are promised for the Day of Account.
53.pickthall: This it is that ye are promised for the Day of Reckoning.
53.yusuf_ali: Such is the Promise made, to you for the Day of Account!
53.shakir: This is what you are promised for the day of reckoning.
53.muhammad_sarwar: This is what they had been promised for the Day of Judgment.
53.mohsin_khan: This it is what you (Al-Muttaqun - the pious) are promised for the Day of Reckoning!
53.arberry: 'This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning;

54.sahih_international: Indeed, this is Our provision; for it there is no depletion.
54.pickthall: Lo! this in truth is Our provision, which will never waste away.
54.yusuf_ali: Truly such will be Our Bounty (to you); it will never fail;-
54.shakir: Most surely this is Our sustenance; it shall never come to an end;
54.muhammad_sarwar: Our provision (for you) will never be exhausted.
54.mohsin_khan: (It will be said to them)! Verily, this is Our Provision which will never finish;
54.arberry: this is Our provision, unto which there is no end.'

55.sahih_international: This [is so]. But indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return -
55.pickthall: This (is for the righteous). And lo! for the transgressors there with be an evil journey's end,
55.yusuf_ali: Yea, such! but - for the wrong-doers will be an evil place of (Final) Return!-
55.shakir: This (shall be so); and most surely there is an evil resort for the inordinate ones;
55.muhammad_sarwar: However, the rebellious ones will have the worst place to return.
55.mohsin_khan: This is so! And for the Taghun (transgressors, disobedient to Allah and His Messenger - disbelievers in the Oneness of Allah, criminals, etc.), will be an evil final return (Fire),
55.arberry: All this; but for the insolent awaits an ill resort,

56.sahih_international: Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the resting place.
56.pickthall: Hell, where they will burn, an evil resting-place.
56.yusuf_ali: Hell!- they will burn therein, - an evil bed (indeed, to lie on)!-
56.shakir: Hell; they shall enter it, so evil is the resting-place.
56.muhammad_sarwar: They will suffer in hell. What a terrible dwelling!
56.mohsin_khan: Hell! Where they will burn, and worst (indeed) is that place to rest!
56.arberry: Gehenna, wherein they are roasted - an evil cradling!

57.sahih_international: This - so let them taste it - is scalding water and [foul] purulence.
57.pickthall: Here is a boiling and an ice-cold draught, so let them taste it,
57.yusuf_ali: Yea, such! - then shall they taste it,- a boiling fluid, and a fluid dark, murky, intensely cold!-
57.shakir: This (shall be so); so let them taste it, boiling and intensely cold (drink).
57.muhammad_sarwar: (They will be told), "This is your recompense.
57.mohsin_khan: This is so! Then let them taste it, a boiling fluid and dirty wound discharges.
57.arberry: All this; so let them taste it - boiling water and pus,

58.sahih_international: And other [punishments] of its type [in various] kinds.
58.pickthall: And other (torment) of the kind in pairs (the two extremes)!
58.yusuf_ali: And other Penalties of a similar kind, to match them!
58.shakir: And other (punishment) of the same kind-- of various sorts.
58.muhammad_sarwar: Taste the scalding water, pus, and other putrid things".
58.mohsin_khan: And other torments of similar kind, all together!
58.arberry: and other torments of the like kind coupled together.

59.sahih_international: [Its inhabitants will say], "This is a company bursting in with you. No welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire."
59.pickthall: Here is an army rushing blindly with you. (Those who are already in the Fire say): No word of welcome for them. Lo! they will roast at the Fire.
59.yusuf_ali: Here is a troop rushing headlong with you! No welcome for them! truly, they shall burn in the Fire!
59.shakir: This is an army plunging in without consideration along with you; no welcome for them, surely they shall enter fire.
59.muhammad_sarwar: Their leaders will be told, "This band will also be thrown headlong with you into hell." Their leaders will exclaim, "May condemnation fall upon them! Let them suffer the torment of fire".
59.mohsin_khan: This is a troop entering with you (in Hell), no welcome for them! Verily, they shall burn in the Fire!
59.arberry: 'This is a troop rushing in with you; there is no Welcome for them; they shall roast in the Fire.'

60.sahih_international: They will say, "Nor you! No welcome for you. You, [our leaders], brought this upon us, and wretched is the settlement."
60.pickthall: They say: Nay, but you (misleaders), for you there is no word of welcome. Ye prepared this for us (by your misleading). Now hapless is the plight.
60.yusuf_ali: (The followers shall cry to the misleaders:) "Nay, ye (too)! No welcome for you! It is ye who have brought this upon us! Now evil is (this) place to stay in!"
60.shakir: They shall say: Nay! you-- no welcome to you: you did proffer it to us, so evil is the resting-place.
60.muhammad_sarwar: Their followers will say, "In fact, it is you who deserve condemnation. It was you who led us to hell, a terrible dwelling".
60.mohsin_khan: (The followers of the misleaders will say): "Nay, you (too)! No welcome for you! It is you (misleaders) who brought this upon us (because you misled us in the world), so evil is this place to stay in!"
60.arberry: They say, 'No, it is you have no Welcome; you forwarded it for us; how evil a stablishment!'

61.sahih_international: They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us - increase for him double punishment in the Fire."
61.pickthall: They say: Our Lord! Whoever did prepare this for us, oh, give him double portion of the Fire!
61.yusuf_ali: They will say: "Our Lord! whoever brought this upon us,- Add to him a double Penalty in the Fire!"
61.shakir: They shall say: Our Lord! whoever prepared it first for us, add Thou to him a double chastisement in the fire.
61.muhammad_sarwar: They will continue saying, "Lord, double the torment of fire for those who led us into this.
61.mohsin_khan: They will say: "Our Lord! Whoever brought this upon us, add to him a double torment in the Fire!"
61.arberry: They say, 'Our Lord, whoso forwarded this for us, give him a double chastisement in the Fire!'

62.sahih_international: And they will say, "Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the worst?
62.pickthall: And they say: What aileth us that we behold not men whom we were wont to count among the wicked?
62.yusuf_ali: And they will say: "What has happened to us that we see not men whom we used to number among the bad ones?
62.shakir: And they shall say: What is the matter with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the vicious?
62.muhammad_sarwar: But why is it that we cannot see men whom we had considered as wicked
62.mohsin_khan: And they will say: "What is the matter with us that we see not men whom we used to count among the bad ones?"
62.arberry: They say, 'How is it with us, that we do not see men here that we counted among the wicked?

63.sahih_international: Is it [because] we took them in ridicule, or has [our] vision turned away from them?"
63.pickthall: Did we take them (wrongly) for a laughing-stock, or have our eyes missed them?
63.yusuf_ali: "Did we treat them (as such) in ridicule, or have (our) eyes failed to perceive them?"
63.shakir: Was it that we (only) took them in scorn, or have our eyes (now) turned aside from them?
63.muhammad_sarwar: and whom we mocked? Have they been rescued or can our eyes not find them?"
63.mohsin_khan: Did we take them as an object of mockery, or have (our) eyes failed to perceive them?"
63.arberry: What, did we take them for a laughing-stock? Or have our eyes swerved away from them?'

64.sahih_international: Indeed, that is truth - the quarreling of the people of the Fire.
